newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent consolidates at lower levels after fall.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent consolidates at lower levels after fall.

text.p: IPE Brent consolidated at lower numbers on Thursday afternoon gaining little direction from NYMEX.
"We are having a breather after yesterday's run-up, which was probably a bit overdone," said one trader.
March Brent was trading at $23.30 a barrel, down 30 cents at 1532 GMT.
Traders said the February contract, which expires at close of business today, was out of the picture.
"Feb looks cut and dried, hardly anyone has positions," said a trader. February Brent was down 19 cents at $23.65 at 1532 GMT.
The energy complex was looking easier following March Brent's failure to break $24.00 a barrel and WTI's inability to breach $26.00.

Gas oil was stronger playing catch-up to crude's late gains on Wednesday, after gas oil had closed. February was up $4.75 at $218.25 a tonne at 1532 GMT. Support also came from forecasts of cold weather in the northeastern United States, a key market for heating oil.
